**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The planner's `likelyAbsent` hint was wrong. The termination provisions exist but are buried under a mis-numbered heading — §§ 13 (Term) and 14 (Termination) are physically inside the block headed "§ 12 INDEMNITY," which is why they didn't surface in the section outline.

**Why this meets the preferred position on both material terms:**

1. **Our convenience right** — § 14 lets Client terminate on nothing more than "a written notice of its election to terminate," with no cause requirement and no early-termination fee or penalty anywhere in the Agreement. Service and fee exposure ends the last day of the month following notice (~30–60 days). That is at or better than the preferred 30-days-without-penalty position.

2. **No Vendor mid-term walk-away** — TrueLink has no convenience right at all. Its only exit is a reciprocal end-of-term non-renewal notice under § 13. The two mid-term triggers in § 13 are for-cause (Client-caused breach of a System/Credit Repository Agreement, or breach of §§ 8a–8c) and cut only §§ 2 and 3, not the whole Agreement.

**Noted in the rationale rather than flagged**, per the playbook's treatment of minor sub-elements:
- No express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees — but § 5a bills monthly in arrears (invoices payable within 15 days), so Client never prepays and the refund mechanic has nothing to operate on.
- TrueLink's non-renewal notice is 30 days, short of the fallback's 90. I declined to flag this because it is a symmetric right Client holds on identical terms in a 12-month (not multi-year) term, and it is not a mid-term walk-away — the rule's actual concern. I flagged it for revisiting if the term is ever extended to multiple years.

One housekeeping item passed along outside this rule: § 2c and § 13 both cross-reference "Section 12" for termination, but the operative mechanic is § 14 — § 12 is indemnity. Worth fixing on a drafting pass, though it doesn't affect the T4C classification.
